title: Earth's Tiny New Mini-Moon Is Staying for Christmas
summary:
Earth has a new tiny neighbor for the holidays: 2026 QQ8, a space rock only about 6 feet wide. Scientists saw it in August 2026, after Earth's gravity caught it in April 2026. The International Astronomical Union's Minor Planet Center shared the news on October 29.

QQ8 is called a mini-moon because it is circling Earth for a short visit. It will stay through December, then drift away in early 2027. Its trip around the sun takes 359 days, or about 0.98 of an Earth year. It swings close to Earth once every ten years.

At its closest, QQ8 will pass about 353,000 miles from Earth, about 110,000 miles farther than the average distance to the moon. Do not worry: even if it headed for Earth, it would likely burn up in the air first.

QQ8 is not the first mini-moon. Research last year said Earth could have as many as six at one time, and many may be pieces of our own moon. The average mini-moon is about 75 centimeters wide, or 30 inches, and stays nine months.
why_it_matters: It shows kids that Earth can catch its own tiny space visitor for the holidays, like a surprise guest staying through Christmas.
